questions.question: What happens if two visible elements share the same `view-transition-name` when a view transition starts?
options: The browser picks the first one in source order and animates it
The transition is skipped, though the DOM update callback still runs
The page throws and the DOM is never updated
questions.explanation: Names must be unique at snapshot time. A duplicate aborts the animation, but the update still happens without the transition.

questions.question: How does a multi-page (same-origin) site opt in to cross-document view transitions?
options: Both pages include `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` in their CSS
Call document.startViewTransition() in a beforeunload handler
Cross-document transitions require a single-page app router
questions.explanation: Cross-document transitions are declared in CSS on both the old and new page, with no JavaScript needed.

questions.question: A `.card` rule sets `animation-timeline: view();` and then, below it, `animation: reveal linear both;`. Why does the scroll effect not work?
options: view() only works on the root element
linear easing is not allowed with scroll timelines
The animation shorthand resets animation-timeline to auto, so the timeline must be declared after it
questions.explanation: Like other shorthands, animation resets its longhands, including animation-timeline. Declare animation-timeline after the shorthand.

questions.question: Which is the safest way to ship scroll-driven animations given uneven browser support?
options: Use them unconditionally; unsupported browsers will polyfill automatically
Wrap them in `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` and animate only transform and opacity
Animate top and height so every browser can render the effect
questions.explanation: Feature-detect with @supports so other browsers get the static layout, and stick to compositor-friendly properties to avoid forcing layout every frame.
